input.quote: EXCEPT FOR LIABILITY ARISING UNDER SECTION 8 OF THIS AGREEMENT, IN NO EVENT SHALL EITHER PARTY'S LIABILITY ARISING OUT OF THIS AGREEMENT OR THE USE OR PERFORMANCE OF THE SOFTWARE EXCEED THE TOTAL AMOUNT ACTUALLY PAID BY CORIO HEREUNDER FOR THE TRANSACTION WHICH THE LIABILITY RELATES TO DURING THE TWELVE (12) MONTHS IMMEDIATELY PRIOR TO THE FILING OF THE CAUSE OF ACTION TO WHICH THE LIABILITY RELATES.
input.rationale: Section 9 caps both parties (mutual) and mutually excludes indirect/consequential damages, and Section 8 (Indemnification) liability is expressly carved out of both the cap and the damages exclusion, so indemnities sit outside the cap. However the clause fails the fallback on two material terms: (i) the cap is not a true twelve-month fee cap because it is limited to amounts paid "FOR THE TRANSACTION WHICH THE LIABILITY RELATES TO", a subset that can fall well below twelve months' fees; and (ii) there are no carve-outs for breach of the Section 10 confidentiality obligations, gross negligence or wilful misconduct (searches return no such language anywhere in the document). Our redline is the shortest fallback-conforming fix: it deletes the per-transaction restriction and adds the three missing carve-outs to the existing exception opener, leaving all other wording verbatim. We have not pursued the preferred USD 1,000,000 floor, data-protection/security, fraud, IP-infringement or payment-obligation elements, which remain open if Commerce One will accept them.
